issues.claim: at $37.91/hour (legal secretary median, NJ, 2025, ×1.25 benefits, our assumption)
issues.problem: Minor labelling imprecision: $37.91 is not the median ($30.33/hr is); it is the median uplifted by 1.25. Same pattern at $97.01/hour (lawyer hourly median is $77.61). The derivation is shown inline, so a reader can follow it, but the figure is described as the median when it is the loaded rate.
issues.fix: Say 'median $30.33/hour, loaded ×1.25 for benefits = $37.91/hour (our assumption)' and 'median $77.61/hour, loaded ×1.25 = $97.01/hour'. Consider labelling the wage year as 'BLS OEWS May 2025 (republished by O*NET)' since the O*NET page itself only says '2025 wage data'.

issues.claim: Case volumes in the three impact calculations (180–240 / 180–360 / 40–200 per year)
issues.problem: These volumes are not from any source; they are the researcher's assumptions (they come from analysis.json's 15–20 and 15–30 enquiries/month and 20–50 matters × 2–4 contacts). They are correctly flagged as 'our assumptions' in the audit, so this is not an error, but the reader should not read them as firm data.
issues.fix: No change required for accuracy. Optionally add a half-line to the first calculation such as 'volumes are our estimate, to be confirmed on the first visit', which is already implied by the closing disclaimer.

issues.claim: a reviewer (c. 2018) describes two cancelled appointments, told closings take priority
issues.problem: The full review text is truncated in the Google Maps interface, so the 'twice' and the closing-priority quote had to be read on a page that mirrors the same four Google reviews. The detail is correct, but the audit does not let a reader check it from the cited Google URL alone.
issues.fix: Optionally add the mirror (lawfirmlookup.com/lawyer/miller-david-a-east-brunswick-nj) beside the Google Maps link in the sources so the quote can be verified without loading Maps.
